subject: Chemistry
title: Solution Classifications & Concentration Temperature Dependence
topics: Solution Classifications: Gaseous, Liquid, and Solid Solutions (Substitutional Brass Cu-Zn, Interstitial Steel)
Concentration Expressions: Molarity (M), Molality (m), Normality (N), Mole Fraction (x_i), % w/w, % w/v, % v/v, ppm
Temperature-Dependent (Volume-based: M, N, %w/v, %v/v) vs Temperature-Independent (Mass-based: m, x_i, %w/w, ppm)
Molality (m) vs Molarity (M) Interconversion Formula: m = (1000 M) / (1000 d - M M_B)
quickSummary: Liquid, gaseous, and solid solutions. Molarity and normality are temperature-dependent (volume expands with T). Molality, mole fraction, and mass % are temperature-independent. m = (1000·M) / (1000·d - M·M_B).
summary: Master solution types, concentration units, thermal dependencies, and interconversion mechanics.

conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 Solution Classifications Matrix

summaryBox.title: Solution Types
summaryBox.takeaway: Homogeneous single-phase mixtures: Gas in gas (Air), Gas in liquid (CO₂ in water), Solid in solid (Brass Cu-Zn, Steel).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SOLUTION CLASSIFICATIONS
                                       │
     ┌─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                                 ▼                                 ▼
GASEOUS SOLUTIONS                 LIQUID SOLUTIONS                  SOLID SOLUTIONS
Solvent: Gas                      Solvent: Liquid                   Solvent: Solid
├── Gas in Gas (Air)              ├── Gas in Liquid (CO₂ in water)  ├── Substitutional (Brass: Cu-Zn)
├── Liquid in Gas (Humidity)      ├── Liquid in Liquid (Ethanol/H₂O)└── Interstitial (Carbon in Steel)
└── Solid in Gas (Camphor in N₂)  └── Solid in Liquid (NaCl in H₂O)
conceptBreakdown.content:
A Solution is a homogeneous single-phase mixture of two or more chemical components. Classified by physical states of solvent and solute:
1. **Gaseous Solutions**: Air ($	ext{O}_2 + 	ext{N}_2$), Chloroform in $	ext{N}_2$ gas, Camphor in $	ext{N}_2$.
2. **Liquid Solutions**: $	ext{CO}_2$ in water (Soda), Ethanol in water, $	ext{NaCl}$ in water.
3. **Solid Solutions**: **Substitutional** (Brass: $	ext{Cu-Zn}$, Bronze: $	ext{Cu-Sn}$) and **Interstitial** (Carbon in iron forming Steel).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Concentration Terms & Thermal Stability
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Concentration Terms & Thermal Stability
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CONCENTRATION EXPRESSIONS MATRIX

• Temperature-Dependent (Volume-based; V expands as T rises ⟹ Concentration decreases):
  ├── Molarity (M = n_solute / V_solution in L)
  ├── Normality (N = Equivalents_solute / V_solution in L)
  └── % w/v and % v/v

• Temperature-Independent (Mass-based; invariant with temperature):
  ├── Molality (m = n_solute / Mass of solvent in kg)
  ├── Mole Fraction (x_i = n_i / Σ n_total)
  └── Mass Percentage (% w/w) and ppm

• Interconversion Formula: m = (1000 × M) / (1000 × d - M × M_B)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Molarity ($M$)**: Decreases as temperature increases because liquids expand ($V \propto T$).
• **Molality ($m$) & Mole Fraction ($x_i$)**: Temperature-independent because mass is invariant with temperature.
• **Interconversion**: $\mathbf{m = \frac{1000 \cdot M}{1000 \cdot d - M \cdot M_B}}$ where $d$ is density ($\text{g/mL}$) and $M_B$ is solute molar mass.

quickRevision: Molarity (M) and Normality (N) depend on temperature.
Molality (m) and Mole fraction (x) are independent of temperature.
Brass is a substitutional solid solution; Steel is interstitial.
